Did Treasury submit Scott Bessent's written answers from the September 15 HFSC hearing, which questions, answers or nonresponses became public, and did the packet disclose GOLD EAGLE's private participants or admission criteria?
Past due, no recordNo source link in the home
October 20, 2026openResearch Return LedgerChairman Hill gave members five legislative days to submit additional written questions to the chair and asked Bessent to respond by October 20, 2026. At the September 17 check, House Event 119546 listed testimony, truth-in-testimony, biography, notice and memorandum, but no QFR packet or responses. Bessent described assistance by large banks and diffusion to smaller banks and service providers but named no fintech company, technology provider or blockchain network and supplied no GOLD EAGLE admission rule. Official launch materials identify participant classes but no complete private roster. Anthropic and Chainguard now supply named private support receipts, and Chainguard describes an Athena-to-Akrites-to-GOLD-EAGLE operating handoff, but those records do not establish formal GOLD EAGLE membership. Historical HFSC annual Treasury hearings have published written answers in the official GPO hearing volume, but the response due date is not a guaranteed public-posting date and a requested answer is not proof of timely or complete receipt. Look again when: On and after October 20, check House Event 119546 and HFSC Event 411218 for transmitted questions, response PDFs or a stated nonresponse; then check GovInfo for the eventual printed hearing record. First test whether the packet answers Huizenga's GOLD EAGLE question using the dedicated dossier's October inspection lens: roster and eligibility, exact operational roles, authority and liability, governance, technical carriage, maintainer/operator control, funding, performance, financial-system joins and the separate model-access boundary. Specifically compare any answer with the known Glasswing, Athena and Akrites rosters and Chainguard's September 15 operating account; do not convert membership in those programs into GOLD EAGLE admission. Use Ripple as the layer-1 stress test: distinguish Ripple Labs, Standard Custody, the proposed Ripple National Trust Bank, XRPL Foundation, validators and ecosystem maintainers; record whether any one is a finder, validator, CNA, maintainer, distributor, critical-infrastructure operator or recipient, and compare any claimed process with the February XRPL Batch vulnerability flow. Record whether 6 U.S.C. 1510 was extended or lapsed after September 30 without assuming GOLD EAGLE itself terminated. Also compare the packet with the four express in-hearing written-follow-up invitations concerning Trump Account escheat, an AI kill switch, TGA use for buybacks and SAR/CTR thresholds.
Date: October 20, 2026

What does the Supreme Court do with Custodia Bank's certiorari petition in No. 26-62, and what later account-access consequence follows?
DatedNo source link in the home
October 28, 2026openResearch Return LedgerThe petition was filed July 10 and docketed July 14. On October 13 the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City filed its brief in opposition. It argues there is no lower-court split, the Board's Payment Account proposal may reshape the dispute, Custodia's all-or-nothing mandamus case did not preserve an APA abuse-of-discretion or constitutional merits challenge, and sections 342 and 248a leave Reserve Banks at least some discretion. Only Kansas City's opposition was visible at the cutoff; no separate Board filing, Custodia reply, distribution, cert disposition, merits ruling or account change had posted. Look again when: Return earlier on a Board response or waiver, Custodia reply, Rule 15.5 waiting-period waiver or docketed distribution. Otherwise check the October 28 paid-list distribution; if distributed then, the published schedule points to the November 13 conference, subject to docket change. Continue through relist, order-list disposition, cert grant/denial, merits schedule or ruling, and any later Board/Reserve Bank/account-database action.

Which new official receipts change any of the Hub's thirty-four tracked crypto-technology families from research, roadmap, announcement, testnet, pilot or availability into named live use, scaled use, stress evidence or an explicit native-token value-capture channel?
DatedNo source link in the home
December 31, 2026openResearch Return LedgerThe September 27 baseline now covers all thirty-four tracked families: twenty deep Field Guide profiles plus fourteen specialist Stack Expansion systems. Stronger receipts include Arc public-mainnet availability, DTCC's limited-production transaction event, Quant's bounded UK live-customer transactions, Ondo/Oasis Pro Fund/SERV membership and case-by-case institutional in-kind conversion, live USDT0 on Stellar, named Solana payment-access products, Kinexys' named KB Kookmin use and existing regulated Securitize operations. Other items remain on different clocks: The Clearing House selected Quant for a future initiative; Partior and LSEG DiSH announced a collaboration; Swift has a ledger ready for initial use with banks preparing pilots; U.S. Bank completed a bounded Stellar pilot; Ethereum upgrades remain roadmap-stage; and several integrations establish support rather than transaction volume. Each record preserves its own missing receipt and token, issued-claim or legal-seat boundary. Look again when: Return earlier when any profile's recorded gate is met: a protocol activates on mainnet; a named pilot becomes standing production; a general service launches; recurring volume, fee, liquidity, reconciliation or recovery data appears; an acquisition closes; an exact operating rulebook or legal-entity route is published; or a contract, wallet, treasury or audited disclosure establishes a required native-token purchase, fee, stake, lock, burn or distribution channel.

Where do FIRE and the FSB third-party toolkit become binding, tested operating controls for common cloud, model, wallet, key, node, bridge, oracle or shared-ledger dependencies?
DatedNo source link in the home
December 31, 2027openResearch Return LedgerFIRE is a final adaptable format with common information items, DPM, XBRL examples and validation rules; each authority still chooses legal scope, trigger, deadline and confidentiality. Research Return Ledger (27)

QuestionWhenStatusHomeDetailDate, source, links
What public legal design emerges from CFTC RIN 3038-AF80, Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets, after OIRA review?
ConditionNo source link in the home
When a condition is metopenResearch Return LedgerOIRA received AF80 on 2026-09-17 and concluded review on 2026-10-02 as Consistent with Change. On 2026-10-05 the CFTC announced an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking for Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions (Regulation CTX) and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets (Regulation CAM). The announcement confirms that CTXs are retail commodity transactions involving crypto assets under CEA section 2(c)(2)(D) and that CAM would be a purpose-built subcategory of designated contract market registration. It seeks input on abuse prevention, crypto-specific contextual guidance and best practices, and says comments will be due 60 days after Federal Register publication. As of the 2026-10-05 EDT cutoff, no AF80 text appears in the Federal Register or Public Inspection feeds, no document-specific Regulations.gov docket was reachable, and no question list, CFR text, exact authority analysis, Commission vote record, venue designation, listed CTX or operating market exists. The proposal advances a voluntary federal route for covered leveraged, margined or financed retail crypto transactions but does not give the CFTC power to require ordinary unleveraged spot crypto to trade on CFTC venues. Look again when: The AF80 ANPRM text, Federal Register notice or document-specific Regulations.gov docket appears; the comment period closes or is extended; the CFTC publishes an NPRM, final rule, vote record, legal analysis or updated actual-delivery interpretation; AF80 appears in the Unified Agenda; an official source links AF80 to AF66; or a named venue seeks or receives CAM designation and lists a CTX.
Home as of: October 5, 2026

Which Iranian institutions are currently eligible or ineligible for SWIFT, with exact BICs and effective times?
ConditionNo source link in the home
When a condition is metopenResearch Return LedgerEU Regulation 267/2012 has, since September 30, 2025, prohibited specialized financial-messaging services to entities in Annexes VIII and IX. Official 2026 corrections supply exact BIC examples including SCERIRTHKSH, SCTSAEA1, SCERIRTH and REFAIRTH, and an implementing regulation identifies the Central Bank of Iran as BMJIIRT1. This establishes list-based legal ineligibility and correct identifiers where supplied, not a complete public operator-connectivity set: SWIFT states that BICs may be connected or non-connected, and its complete connectivity data resides in SwiftRef. No public SWIFT execution list through October 5 reconciles every Iranian institution and disconnection timestamp. Do not assume: that all Iranian banks are disconnected, that BIC existence proves connectivity or that a legal listing supplies the actual operator execution time. Look again when: A named operator-connectivity change or authoritative current directory becomes public. Look for: SWIFT, an EU or Belgian authority, a named-bank notice or authorized SwiftRef evidence supplies the institution, BIC, connectivity state and execution time.

What exact Commission legal object creates any SEC innovation exemption, under what authority, conditions and duration, and who is the first admitted participant?
ConditionNo source link in the home
When a condition is metopenResearch Return LedgerSEC Release 34-106402, File No. 4-927, is the effective Commission legal object. Under Exchange Act section 36(a)(1), it grants separate temporary conditional exemptions from the definitions of exchange for qualifying Tokenized Securities Venues and dealer for qualifying own-account liquidity providers through September 17, 2031. BTCS says Imperium submitted the Covered Firm notification and published disclosures, making it the first publicly identified prospective reliance filer located; the order does not make that an admission or approval, and Imperium expressly has not commenced the activity because no qualifying TSV is operating. Do not assume: that legal permission, notification, admission, venue operation and actual use are the same state. Look again when: The first actual reliance and operation appears. Look for: A TSV publishes its initial Notice and begins operating, or a Covered Firm records qualifying activity, with identity, asset, pool, participant, trade, record, custody, clearing, settlement and public transaction data kept separate.

ConditionNo source link in the home
When a condition is metopenResearch Return LedgerAct No. 64 was promulgated July 23 and a narrow enforcement subset commenced August 12. Through October 5, the FSA's official Diet-bill and current publication surfaces supplied no Cabinet order fixing the main commencement date and no crypto-specific implementing package expressly tied to Act No. 64. The May 22 crypto-intermediary rules implement the 2025 Payment Services Act amendment, the August 7 FSA reorganization creates an administrative owner, and the September 15 FIEA orders concern digital bonds, foreign venture funds and paperless depositary receipts; none closes this return. Do not assume: that the full reform is effective or that exchange re-registration, asset treatment, 20-percent tax activation or ETF permission follows from nearby but different legal objects. ConditionNo source link in the home
When a condition is metopenResearch Return LedgerFinal core rule released October 21; OCC says intake is not yet open pending OMB approval. Existing issuers may seek written prior-approval waivers with substantially complete applications pending on or before January 18. Revised reporting remains subject to OMB approval; first weekly report date January 25, 2027 (filing January 27), first quarterly report date March 31 (filing by April 30). Technical schemas, dictionary and edit checks are promised before implementation. The full90page reporting notice and selected revised instructions have now been read. They preserve a PRA/OMB process and reveal named capital-rule/instruction questions for later clarification. This document reading is not a fresh check of OMB or intake status. Wave6 completes the application notice and domestic approval text: no deemed-complete backstop; persistently incomplete applications returned without decision after60days; conditional issuer approval is not routine two-stage chartering but can carry precommencement conditions. Footnote165 defers the120day clock until the later of effectiveness or substantial completeness. These are source-reading clarifications, not a new intake or issuer decision check. Wave7 separates Treasury comparability, OCC foreign registration, four U.S.liquidity routes and loss-of-permission clocks; no direct general foreign capital/backstop mandate is imposed here. Foreign schedule-specific drafting questions remain. These findings do not establish a country determination, reciprocal arrangement, registration or new live intake status. Wave8 confirms the legal capital formulas: all DTAs net of allowances and required backstop less qualifying debt. Narrower DTA instruction and surplus-backstop reporting classification remain implementation discrepancies. It verifies parent loss addback, absence of a source-of-strength requirement/expectation, and prior approval for uninsured-trust-bank elections; no actual election, deficiency or new intake status is established. Wave9 confirms reserve fee relief includes excess designated reserves without a1–5percent cap, while foreign assessments initially use cost-based supervisory hours. It identifies a custody ScheduleC/E crosswalk mismatch and stale derivative item references; exact key-valuation convention in the checked custody field remains unestablished. No current fee notice, actual invoice or live regulatory status was refreshed. Wave10 completes main-page reading and reproduces corePRA/economic arithmetic without validating model assumptions. Reporting notice10458hours explicitly overlaps the89137coretotal. Retained seven-day extension text, capital equation sign and bank-fee component difference are recorded. This is not a publication, OMB, live-rate, issuer or actual-cost refresh. Wave11 reconciles all37added/amended section records and19numbered amendment instructions, preserving39classified source issues and an additional state-transition capital-reference question. This is a released-text audit, not current consolidated law, official correction or actual relief. Completed synthesis now consolidates all721main pages and both notices. The research reading is complete; this return remains open only for future external publication/ICR/intake/permission/correction/operating receipts, not unfinished campaign pages. No fresh live-status inference is made. Look again when: An official Federal Register publication/citation appears; OMB approves the application or reporting collection; OCC announces intake; an issuer receives a substantially complete application determination, approval or actual transition waiver; reporting technical specifications are published; or a named uninsured trust bank receives a part 15 capital election. Check the effective-date transition by January 18, 2027 if no earlier trigger occurs. On finalized instructions/schemas or OCC clarification, reconcile DTA deduction scope, required-versus-reported backstop deduction, and foreign/reduced-detail schedule applicability. On finalized reporting instructions or an official assessment crosswalk, reconcile custody ScheduleC versusEItem19, derivative3a/3b references versus5a/5b, and issuance-key valuation inputs. Published annual fee parameters or actual foreign supervisory estimates/invoices provide later cost evidence. An official correction or updated impact analysis can resolve the seven-day redemption description and unreconciled bank-fee savings component. Final approved ICR/supporting statements can reconcile application burden allocations without double counting reporting estimates. An official correction/clarification may settle15.15(b)(3)(iii) reference to15.41(a)(1)(ii) (definition) versus the monetary requirement in(a)(1)(i).

What's still uncertain

  • Past due means the date passed and the home holds no record dated on or after it. Work may have happened outside the library.
  • Most Innovation Exemption and Fed-proposal clocks count from an event (publication, notice, filing) that has not happened, so they have no calendar date yet.
  • Open questions carry their master's check-by date, not a date of their own.
  • Return Ledger questions are included when their question or tags name a crypto subject; the full ledger is on the government waiting-on page.

  • Masters: genius_act_milestones.json, stablecoins.json (coins' open questions; the Fed's GENIUS proposals), crypto_companies_and_networks.json, fed_access_and_charters.json, crypto_rules.json (check_by and open_questions).

What first authoritative objects move either ARK's Exchange Class or Tokenized Class from exemptive permission into effective registration, venue admission, issuance, trading, settlement, accounting reconciliation and repeated operation? — saved earlier record

Preserved from Library edition r27. This record is historical because its current identity or content was not proved equivalent; it is not silently assigned to a new record.

record date: 2026-10-23

When
October 23, 2026
Status
open
Home
Research Return Ledger
Detail
Order IC-36333 supplies immediately effective conditional exemptive permission for the architecture. As of September 30, no Tokenized Class registration, named blockchain, transfer agent/tokenization agent, wallet system, ATS, stablecoin rail, launch or transaction receipt was located. Class X registration effectiveness was delayed by Form 486BXT to October 23, 2026; intended TXSE listing and ticker ARKV do not yet establish admission or live trading. Look again when: Return earlier if ARK files a Tokenized Class registration statement or names its DLT, transfer-agent, wallet, ATS, cash or custody stack; if TXSE admits Class X or publishes a launch notice; or if an official filing, venue record, chain record, financial statement or auditor report evidences issuance, trade, settlement, repurchase, reconciliation or repeated operation.

Library files: Research Packages/SEC Accredited Investor Credential Notices 2026-09-30/ARK_VENTURE_FUND_TOKENIZED_CLASS_CONTROL_MAP_2026-09-30.md; Research Packages/SEC Accredited Investor Credential Notices 2026-09-30/ARK_VENTURE_FUND_TOKENIZED_CLASS_CONTROL_MAP_2026-09-30.md

Does XRP become recurring invisible bridge inventory rather than an optional protocol capability? — saved earlier record

Preserved from Library edition r27. This record is historical because its current identity or content was not proved equivalent; it is not silently assigned to a new record.

record date: 2026-10-14

When
When a condition is met
Status
open
Home
Research Return Ledger
Detail
October 14 targeted update: Evernorth identifies a 473 million XRP treasury and named Ripple, Kraken, Coinbase and BitGo as execution partners, planning initial strategies in Q4 and later native lending when activated and proven. This establishes a substantial institutional capital supplier and intended deployment, but not deployed/borrowed amounts, recurring XRP payment intermediation or financed market-maker inventory economics. Ripple Prime collateral acceptance and BNY cash/custody relationships do not establish XRP or RLUSD use in FICC CIL. Prior route-level evidence limits remain; do not confuse treasury holdings with required operational inventory. Look again when: Ripple, a regulated liquidity provider, custodian, market maker or institutional customer publishes route-level XRP intermediation and inventory economics. Look for: Identify recurring permitted route share, unlike-asset or FX path, realized depth/slippage, gross and net inventory, borrowed amount, average holding time, turnover, financing cost, collateral haircut and hedge treatment. Evernorth publishes executed deployments and borrowers: distinguish lending/market-making demand from directional exposure and identify amount, duration, financing and hedge economics.

Library files: Research Packages/Monetary Cross-Cuts/Authority Through the Adapter 2025-2026/ROUTE_ANCHOR_INVENTORY_INDICATOR_FALSIFIER_AND_RETURN_LEDGER_2026-2028.md; Research Packages/Fintech and Private Rails/EVERNORTH_RIPPLE_BNY_APPCHAIN_AND_CIL_COMPARISON_2026-10-14.md
